## TL;DR

A review report whose `## Bugs` section opened with `None found` but then listed the
things the reviewer had checked as unordered bullets was parsed as "still lists
blocking bugs", so `repoos landable` stayed red on the `review-verdict` check and
close-out refused a clean task (#1077 was the live example). The root cause was in
`src/core/review-report-sections.ts`: `isEmptyReviewSection` skipped "none" lines but
returned `false` (non-empty / blocking) for *any* other list-marker line, so bullets
that were commentary read as findings.

I implemented the fix suggested by the task: when the first substantive line of a
section is a none statement, later **unordered** bullets (and plain prose) are treated
as commentary, while **numbered** items (`1.`, `2)`) and **bold-labelled** findings
(`**Bug:** …`) after that opener still block — i.e. fail closed on mixed content.
Sections that do not open with a none statement keep the original rule that any
list-marker line is a finding. Table-driven tests cover each acceptance criterion, the
reviewer prompts in both `DEFAULT_AGENTS` and the shared `reviewMission` template gained
one line telling reviewers to list what they checked under `## Edge cases` (or a heading
of its own), and `docs/close-out-pipeline.md` records the rule.

## Work and rationale

The change is concentrated in `src/core/review-report-sections.ts`. `isEmptyReviewSection`
now tracks two pieces of state across a section's lines: `sawFirstSubstantive` and
`openedWithNone`. On the first substantive line it tests `firstLineIsNoneOpener`, which
returns true when the line is a none statement *or* a bold label whose value is
none-ish (`**Bugs:** None found`). If that opener matches, `openedWithNone` is set and
the loop continues. Once `openedWithNone` is true, a list-marker line only blocks when
it is a numbered item (`NUMBERED_LIST_MARKER`) or carries a bold-labelled non-none
finding; otherwise it is commentary. The pre-existing behaviour for sections without
that opener is untouched: any list marker is a finding.

I kept the accepted rule deliberately simple and documented it in the JSDoc above the
function so the "fail closed" boundary is legible to the next reader: a numbered or
bold-labelled finding after `None found` means the reviewer did list something, so the
section blocks rather than silently pass. That is the safer default — a false
"commentary" verdict would let a real bug land, while the failure mode we are fixing
(commentary mis-read as findings) only blocked a *clean* task.

Two things mattered beyond the parser:

1. **The rule needs to be applied everywhere the section parser is used.** Because
   `extractReviewReportSections` calls `isEmptyReviewSection` for Bugs, Edge cases and
   Suggestions through `sectionContent`, the fix propagates to every consumer at once:
   `reviewReportHasBlockingBugs` (used by `src/server/landable.ts` `blockingBugs`,
   `src/core/landable.ts`'s `review-verdict` check and `src/core/decision-digest.ts`),
   plus `reviewFindingsMessage`/`unresolvedReviewFindingsBlock` in the auto-bounce
   path. I verified this by exercising `reviewReportHasBlockingBugs` directly against a
   realistic full report shaped like the #1077 failure and confirming the Bugs section
   extracts to `undefined`.

2. **The reviewer prompt should steer writers away from the shape entirely.** The task
   asked for one line in the reviewer prompt. The built-in reviewer instructions live in
   `src/core/config.ts` (`DEFAULT_AGENTS`) and the per-pass mission template lives in
   `src/server/review.ts` (`reviewMission`). I updated both, since a review is produced
   from the mission template but the agent's standing instructions also shape its
   format. Each got a line telling the reviewer to put the checklist of what it checked
   under `## Edge cases` or its own heading, never under `## Bugs`.

## Approaches tried

- **Parsing rule placement.** The task offered a rule and I followed its shape rather
  than inventing a looser one. An alternative was "`None found` anywhere in the section
  makes it empty", but that would wrongly pass `None found\n\n1. real crash` as clean.
  The chosen rule (opener only, numbered/bold still block) keeps fail-closed semantics.
- **Test placement.** I followed the task's steer and put the table tests next to the
  existing section-parser tests in `src/ui-app/tests/review-report-sections.test.ts`,
  adding two phrase tables (`NONE_OPENER_COMMENTARY`, `NONE_OPENER_MIXED_FINDINGS`) run
  against `isEmptyReviewSection`, `extractReviewReportSections` (all three sections) and
  `reviewReportHasBlockingBugs`. I updated the existing `approval-policy.test.ts` and
  `landable-gather.test.ts` tables too, so the whole class of behaviour is pinned in the
  suites that exercise the landable and approval paths.
- **Prompt-line test coverage.** Rather than trusting the prompt edit, I asserted it in
  `default-agent-prompts.test.ts` for both the reviewer role prompt and the shared mission
  prompt, so a later edit that drops the guidance fails a test.

## Challenges and blockers

- **Docs table placement.** My first docs edit inserted the new paragraph *inside* the
  `repoos landable` check table in `docs/close-out-pipeline.md`, between two table rows,
  which would have broken the table's rendering. I moved it below the table, one line.
- **Standalone vitest for one file.** `bunx vitest run src/ui-app/tests/repo-guide.test.ts`
  fails with "Install @vitejs/plugin-vue to handle .vue files" without the repo's test
  wrapper. Pre-existing (the file imports a `.vue` component); the same file passes under
  `bun run test`. I left it alone and did not weaken the test.
- **Recovering from a crashed turn.** The previous session ended in an error before any
  handoff, leaving the fix committed as WIP checkpoints. On resume I found the
  implementation already present and correct against every criterion, so the work was
  verification, not rewriting.
- **Main had moved 35 commits ahead** (including the #1092 release). A naive
  `git diff main --stat` showed those as branch changes purely because the merge-base
  predated them; merging `main` in collapsed the diff to only this task's files. I rebuilt
  before the scoped check so the staleness gate would not fire.
- **The first scoped check failed for environmental reasons, not logic.** Main was merged
  into the branch *while* the check ran (`worktree-drift`: HEAD moved `2112bf99`→`2c84528e`),
  invalidating the check's tree. Two wall-clock timing tests timed out in the same run and
  the run lost `~/.repoos/agent-run-tmp` mid-flight (an `ENOENT` cascaded across files).
  Re-running those two files alone on the merged tree passed all 33 tests — load flakes.
  The remedy was rebuild + re-run on stable HEAD, not a code change.
- No human-gated steps were needed.

## Key learnings

- **A "none" statement and a findings list can share a section**; the disambiguator is
  what *follows* the opener, not the opener alone. Numbered and bold-labelled entries are
  strong signals of a real finding; unordered bullets after `None found` are almost always
  the reviewer's checklist.
- **Fixing the shared parser is the cheapest route to fixing every consumer.** The three
  call sites named in the task (`landable.ts`, `core/landable.ts`, `decision-digest.ts`)
  all flow through `extractReviewReportSections`, so one well-scoped change in
  `isEmptyReviewSection` fixed the board, the CLI and the digest together.
- **Prompt guidance and parser leniency are complementary.** Making the parser forgiving
  fixes the immediate block, but telling reviewers where to put their checklist prevents
  the ambiguity at the source. Doing both — and testing both — is what makes the fix
  durable.
